prompt: Simplify: $(x^2)^4$. Write your answer as a power of $x$.
hint: $(x^2)^4$ means four copies of $x^2$ multiplied: $x^2 \cdot x^2 \cdot x^2 \cdot x^2$.

hints.text: $(x^2)^4$ means four copies of $x^2$ multiplied: $x^2 \cdot x^2 \cdot x^2 \cdot x^2$.
Each $x^2$ carries 2 copies of $x$, and there are 4 groups: $2 \times 4$ copies.

explanation: A power of a power is copies of copies: 4 groups, each holding 2 copies of $x$.
So $(x^2)^4 = x^8$. Power rule: multiply the exponents.

alternativeExplanations.title: Add them up with the product rule
steps: Unroll it: (x²)⁴ = x² · x² · x² · x².
Multiplying powers adds exponents: 2 + 2 + 2 + 2 = 8, so x⁸.

alternativeExplanations.title: Egg-carton picture
steps: Picture 4 cartons, each holding 2 eggs. Every egg is one copy of x being multiplied.
Total eggs: 4 × 2 = 8, so the answer is x⁸.
